reading.text:
UNIT rem_diag_mono. Passage: Remark 2.8 (lines 460-469): the pointwise G-monotonicity condition
(the inequality of (2.7) without expectations at every fixed theta,theta' in H, mu,mu' in P_2(H))
applied at theta=Theta(omega), theta'=Theta'(omega), mu=Law Theta, mu'=Law Theta', and taking
expectations, gives Assumption 2.5. Clause adds: under (2.3) and Assumption 2.3.

Faithful statement: standing basis, any m,n,G, sigma-finite nu. Hypotheses: coefficients jointly
Borel with (2.3) (so the pairings are random variables), Assumption 2.3 (so they are integrable
along diagonal pairs), and the pointwise interior inequality
<db,G^T dy>+<dsigma,G^T dz>_F+<-df,G dx>+int<dh(e),G^T du(e)>nu <= -beta1(|G^T dy|^2+|G^T dz|^2+
||G^T du||^2) - beta2 |G dx|^2 for (a.e.) t and ALL theta,theta' in H, mu,mu' in P_2(H)
(free, not only diagonal). Conclusion: the expected interior inequality (2.7) for a.e. t and all
diagonal pairs, with the same beta1,beta2. If "gives Assumption 2.5" is formalised as the whole
Assumption 2.5, the terminal condition and constants constraints must be hypotheses too (the
pointwise notion in the remark concerns (2.7) only). Pointwise required at every t would be a
slightly stronger hypothesis than a.e. t; a.e. t is the faithful one.

Standing setting (paper §2), shared by every proposition below: a filtered probability space
satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T>0, dimensions n,m,d>=1, a d-dim Brownian motion W and an
independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a
countably generated (E,E) (so L^2(nu;R^j) separable); the filtration is the usual augmentation of
the one generated by W, N and an independent F_0. H = R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x L^2(nu;R^m) with the
HILBERT (l^2-sum) norm |x|^2+|y|^2+|z|_F^2+||u||^2 (not a sup norm); W_2 on P_2(H) w.r.t. that norm.
Coefficients b,sigma,f: [0,T] x H x P_2(H) -> R^n, R^{n x d}, R^m; h: [0,T] x H x P_2(H) -> L^2(nu;R^n);
g: R^n x P_2(R^n) -> R^m; deterministic, jointly Borel; h Borel into L^2(nu;R^n) (2.3).
Diagonal input at t: (Theta, Law Theta) with Theta in L^2(Omega,F_t;H).
Ass 2.2: xi_0 in L^2(F_0), origin values b(.,0,delta_0), sigma(.,0,delta_0), h(.,0,.,delta_0),
 f(.,0,delta_0) in L^2(0,T).
Ass 2.3: exists L>=0: for a.e. t, all diagonal pairs, |db|+|dsigma|_F+||dh||+|df| <= L(|dX|+|dY|+|dZ|_F
 +||dU||+W_2(mu,mu')) a.s.; and for all X_T,X'_T in L^2(F_T), |dg_T|<=L(|dX_T|+W_2(rho,rho')) a.s.
Ass 2.4: G in R^{m x n} full rank; ||G|| operator norm; c_G = s_min(G)^{-2}.
Ass 2.5: terminal E<dg_T, G dX_T> >= alpha E|G dX_T|^2 for all X_T,X'_T in L^2(F_T); interior (2.7)
 for a.e. t and all diagonal pairs, with alpha,beta1,beta2>=0, alpha+beta1>0, beta1+beta2>0,
 beta1>0 if m<n, alpha,beta2>0 if m>n.
(2.12) weighted margin, (2.13) unweighted margin (m=n): extra -c E[...] on the right of (2.7).
Solution: Theta=(X,Y,Z,U) in S := S^2 x S^2 x H^2_W x H^2_N (cadlag adapted X,Y; predictable Z, U
 L^2(nu)-valued), both identities of (1.1) a.s. for every t, h at the predictable tuple
 (Theta_t^-, mu_t^-), mu, mu^- the Borel law flows of Lemma A.1. Weak class H^2 (L^2(0,T) cadlag
 adapted X,Y). Equality: X,Y indistinguishable, Z dt x dP-a.e., U dt x dP x nu-a.e.

comparison.text:
rem_diag_mono vs my reading.
- Setting: standing basis, any n, m, d, T, G, beta1, beta2 (reals, not required >= 0), coefficients
  with JointBorel (2.3).
- Hypothesis: for a.e. t in [0,T] and ALL theta, theta' in H, mu, mu' in P2(H), the pointwise
  inequality pairing27 <= -beta1(|G^T dy|^2 + |G^T dz|^2 + ||G^T du||^2) - beta2 |G dx|^2 (a.e. t, as
  in my reading). OK.
- Conclusion part 2 (the printed claim, "under (2.3) and Assumption 2.3"): for every L with
  Assumption23, Mono27At for a.e. t: the expected diagonal inequality (2.7) with integrable pairing,
  same constants. The remark's "gives Assumption 2.5" concerns the interior condition (2.7) (the
  pointwise notion is defined only for (2.7)); stating (2.7) rather than the whole Assumption 2.5 is
  the faithful reading. OK.
- Conclusion part 1 (extra): without Ass 2.3, the positive part of the pairing has finite
  expectation and, when the pairing is integrable, (2.7) holds. An additional true strengthening.
- Witness rem_affine_hypotheses: Ex 5.1(i) at nu = delta_0 satisfies the pointwise form and
  Ass 2.3. OK.
Verdict: broader (extra conjunct without Ass 2.3; constants not restricted to be >= 0).

verdict.detail:
Broader than printed: beta1, beta2 range over all reals, and the proposition adds a first conjunct
(without Assumption 2.3: the positive part of the pairing has finite expectation and (2.7) holds
whenever the pairing is integrable). The printed claim is the second conjunct at beta1, beta2 >= 0:
under (2.3), the pointwise inequality of (2.7) at a.e. t and all points and laws, and Assumption 2.3
with some L, the expected diagonal inequality (2.7) (Mono27At, pairing integrable) holds for a.e.
t with the same constants.

author_review.disagreements:
No disagreement of substance; the author itself says the proposition "is broader than either reading
alone". I label the verdict "broader" (extra conjunct without Assumption 2.3, beta1, beta2 not
restricted to be >= 0) rather than "faithful".
